title: Keep the desk's book on the desk's thread

blocks.text: The quoting desk keeps its rates in a `Book` that isn't thread-safe. The design gives the book to one thread, the desk's own executor, so that nothing needs a lock: every call into the book runs there. Quotes come from the market-data adapters as `CompletableFuture`s. When an adapter has the rate cached, the future is already complete; otherwise one of the adapter's own threads completes it later.

The desk passed every test, where the adapters are stubs with every rate cached. In production its book has twice lost a rate during a busy minute, and a thread dump caught an adapter thread inside `Book.apply`.

items: `onQuote(...)`: put the quote into the book once it has arrived, and return at once;
`rate(...)`: answer with the book's rate for a pair.

blocks.text: When you're done, every call into the book runs on the desk's thread, whether the quote was already complete, arrives later from an adapter, or is being read. About three lines in total.
The tests give the desk a single-thread executor named `desk` and a book that records which thread made each call.

cases.says: a quote completed later on an adapter's thread is applied to the book, and the desk then reports it
a quote that is already complete is applied to the book, and the desk then reports it
the desk reports no rate for a pair that was never quoted
a quote completed on an adapter's thread is applied to the book on the desk's thread
a quote that is already complete is applied on the desk's thread, not on the caller's
a request for a rate reads the book on the desk's thread

origin.section: State Confined to One Thread Needs No Lock, Until a Callback Runs Somewhere Else

concepts: A callback attached with a non-async method runs on the thread that completes the future, or at once on the attaching thread when the future is already complete, so state confined to an owner thread must be handed back through the owner's executor.
Reads of confined state run on the owner thread too, not only writes.
